chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Nostalgia radio and the new swing audience
summary: They discuss WNEW, WEVD, Phil Schaap and how old songs sound new to younger listeners.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: But I must say, on most of these nostalgia radio programs I listen to, it seems to be a nostalgia for its own sake, not because the music is only of a superior quality.
Right, on the other hand . . .
Most of the things that are played are from the white swing tradition.
Yeah, right.
You really don't hear too much black performers except a few selected.
Well there isn't anything being recorded now.
No, I'm referring to radio stations that have a nostalgia policy.
There are only one or two people
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
that I know, one person in particular and that's Phil Schaap.
That's a jazz program.
Right.
But on commercial radio stations WEVD, I think, I think that's basically a Jewish radio station . . .
Yeah, Danny Stiles.
Yeah, Danny Stiles, that's the one I'm thinking of. Okay, and now on WNEW-AM they are playing swing.
Is that Jim Lowe?
Different disc jockeys at different times of the day.

Well, WNYC, the City Station, I was there the day before yesterday and we were talking about this and the young man that was interviewing me, I don't even remember his name, but the station is going jazz in a few days. And they're not only playing old records which have been souped up, you know, there are some recording studio bands, orchestras that are actually doing some of the older arrangements now. I mean they're

recording them now. So everything you hear, they may be the old songs and the old arrangements but they're being recorded now. And of course, you see, recently there has been this upsurge interest in jazz especially on the college circuit and there are alot of young musicians in colleges that are rehearsing and playing these big arrangements, the Glenn Miller arrangements, the Count Basie arrangements, all those earlier things.
Yes.
